person: Hana Kowalczyk is 34 and runs a one-person online shop from her studio in Oregon. She sells ceramics and linen, and last fall she added a small gift-jar line, repacking a supplier's almond butter into 4 oz jars under her own label. A recall notice from that supplier landed in her inbox, and she has never traced a lot before. She does everything herself, wants to know right away whether this is built for a shop her size, and will answer questions from memory but not from a report she has to download. She is nervous about anything that looks official and does not want to send a false alarm to a customer.
stated_up_front: Okay, my almond butter supplier sent a recall email and I honestly don't know what to do with it. I only have a handful of wholesale accounts and a distributor, so is this even something you can sort out for a shop my size? I have orders to pack, so tell me what you need from me.

facts.truth: Their almond butter lots ALM-2608-14, -15 and -16, per the first email; a follow-up email clarified that -13 and -17 are clear.
Lots -13 through -17 are all in her studio pantry, about 2 tubs of each, so three need holding and two do not.
Batch J-0914 used lot -14, J-0921 used -15, J-0930 used -16, J-0907 used -13, and J-0938 used -17. Her cinnamon honey jar batch has no almond butter in it.
Leftover almond butter from lot -15 was stirred into a cocoa spread batch, C-1002, so that batch is affected even though it is a different product.

facts.about: Her direct customers who got an affected batch
facts.truth: Five: Northwoods Gift Supply (the distributor), Fern & Fig boutique, Clatsop Corner Cafe, Bluebird Home, and Tilly's Pantry (which got the cocoa spread).

facts.about: A customer who should be left alone
facts.truth: Harbor Street Goods only received the J-0907 and cinnamon honey batches, which are unaffected.
A Fern & Fig reorder of J-0930 is packed but still sitting on her shelf, due to ship October 26.
Northwoods Gift Supply resells to about a dozen shops on its own. Their contract says Northwoods tells them, and she has no list of them.
The supplier email came October 20, and today is October 23.
She tracks lots in an Airtable base she set up herself, and her written recall procedure is a one-page Google Doc.

unknowns: Whether a shop as small as hers is legally required to notify customers or hold lots under the FDA rules, or how fast.
What the recall's class or reason means in the FDA's terms.
Whether she has to tell the distributor's own customers herself or only the distributor.
Whether the recall rules cover the cocoa spread, which only got a small amount of the rework.
